column3: Direct parallel: succession follows removal and opens action-examination; it also admits a renewed-opportunity reading.
Adds the historical-outcome lens for reading earlier wrongdoing, without the succession or testing clause.
Only a broad earth-and-signs setting; it does not develop succession or accountable action.
A second, now redundant, call to inspect the outcome of deniers.
Adds that wrongful earning has a consequential return, clarifying why deeds after succession matter.
Frames the earthly setting itself as a test distinguished by quality of action.
Directly joins earthly succession, differentiated standing, and trial in what is given.
Supplies the immediately preceding pattern of ruined generations that makes the new succession intelligible.
Adds the possibility that deeds lose their standing, sharpening the stakes of the action test.
Directly reiterates earthly succession while individuating the consequence of rejection.
Shows that prior strength and accumulation do not prevent removal, qualifying inherited security.
A generic reward-for-action parallel, already covered more specifically by earlier cards.
Another historical-outcome formulation, redundant after the earlier outcome cards.
Adds irreversible personal accountability after wrongdoing, rather than a new succession pattern.
A generic positive-action outcome, adding little after the prior action-and-recompense cards.
Establishes recurrent replacement by another generation, but without the focus's evaluative dimension.
Adds surviving dwellings as evidence through which later people encounter prior destruction.
Makes replacement conditional on turning away and distinguishes the replacing community from the former one.
Narratively joins rescue, installation as successors, and the fate of those who denied warning.
Adds self-directed consequence for guidance and deviation, a secondary account of responsibility.
Recasts being made successors as entrusted use of what one holds, with a concrete response.
Merely repeats later generations after earlier ones, now redundant.
Separates each side's liability, supporting responsibility without identifying a successor transition.
A generic favorable result of faithful action, with little further specificity.
Contrasts prior earthly establishment and abundance with destruction for wrongdoing, followed by another generation.
Repeats separate liability with no further connection to succession or examination.
Contrast evidence only; it sets a boundary around nullified action rather than positively supporting the focus.
Adds the adverse successor case: a later generation can fail the inherited responsibility.
Concerns fidelity to received discourse, only indirectly related to action under succession.
Offers a secondary replacement/recompense sense, not a generational earthly succession.
Shows harmful conduct after rescue and a later accounting of what was done, a close counterpattern.
Adds finality of destroyed generations but no new account of the successors' conduct.
Uses succession in a hypothetical nonhuman setting, so it contributes little to the focus's historical pattern.
Pairs the focus on human action with divine creation of acts, preserving a tension rather than resolving it.
Reiterates total erasure of prior generations, already well established by earlier cards.
Directly parallels the not-being-left-unexamined formulation and explicit divine awareness of action.
The seeing vocabulary concerns changing signs, not the focus's examination of successors' deeds.
Directly presents making people successors in the earth after relief from distress.
Contrast evidence only; it marks a boundary around invalidated work, not positive support.
Adds comprehensive divine awareness of deeds within the earthly realm, but not a successor transition.
A specific destructive outcome that is redundant with the earlier historical-outcome evidence.
Celestial imagery has no material link to succession or the assessment of action.
Parallels communal appointment, witnessing, and a discriminating test of response.
Creation and provision in the earth do not add a successor or action-assessment relation.
Its contrast route supplies only a boundary; the surveillance image is not positive evidence for the focus.
Adds return and disclosure of deeds in a distinct moral setting, secondary to the successor frame.
Adds the severe negative endpoint in which performed works are rendered without durable result.
A broad accountability reference without a distinct succession or testing contribution.
Directly describes later dwelling in the land after others, with a moral condition attached.
Divine custodianship is only a background parallel to the focus's agency and observation.
The making of a garden is too remote from generational succession or tested conduct.
Another general historical-outcome call, fully redundant by this point.
Contrast evidence only; it bounds presumptuous claims and does not positively develop the focus.
Supplies earthly establishment and provision, together with the possibility of an inadequate response.
Ultimate presentation before God is too general here to add to the action-examination pattern.
Directly depicts succession after a prior people, settlement in the land, and a prohibition on corrupt use.
Marks a boundary between a messenger's lack of access to deeds and the focus's divine examination.
A further, redundant historical-outcome formula.
Generic preservation of the reward for good action, already covered more specifically.
The earth reference concerns physical formation, not succession or accountable conduct.
Adds destruction of settlements for wrongdoing and an appointed endpoint, but repeats the prior-removal side.
Provides an alternative route to inheritance and leadership in the land for the oppressed.
A sign and mercy formulation unrelated to succession or testing of a community's deeds.
Another historical destruction-and-outcome card with no new successor dimension.
A general distribution of recompense by deeds, now redundant.
Directly links promised earthly succession after earlier people with an ongoing condition of worship and non-association.
Provides an origin-level earthly khalifah frame and the possibility of corruption, not the later replacement scene.
Reiterates the failure of stronger earlier peoples, with little beyond existing outcome evidence.
A geographic scene without a relevant transition, test, or deed-account.
Its historical-outcome instruction repeats an already saturated line of evidence.
The loss-of-works question is only a fragment and adds little after the fuller work-outcome cards.
Directly recalls succession after Noah's people and added capacity, though the pattern is now redundant.
Pairs righteous action with divine knowledge of deeds, a direct but secondary examination parallel.

Corruption in the earth is present, but there is no succession or evaluative transition.
A late repetition of traveling to inspect earlier outcomes.
Divine awareness of deeds appears in an unrelated setting and adds little after closer parallels.
A further power-and-destruction outcome card, redundant with the earlier historical cases.
A generic best-deed recompense formulation, already represented.
Another redundant invitation to inspect the fate of stronger earlier people.
Adds graded fulfillment according to deeds, clarifying that action has differentiated consequences.
Creation and resurrection are not a material contribution to succession or its test.
Offers precedent as warning, but only indirectly and without a successor relation.
Revival of the earth is a different renewal pattern, not generational replacement.
Repentant action supplies a generic renewal possibility but no specific successor frame.
Repeats the historical fate of developed earlier peoples without adding to the established pattern.
Warns that conduct can invalidate works, adding a conditional negative stake to action under responsibility.
The isolated looking verb has no contextual relation to the focus.
A terse deed-based recompense reference, entirely generic by this point.
The earth appears in a ransom scenario, not in succession or examination.
Adds testing in what communities are given and a final disclosure of differences, a parallel communal trial frame.
The making here concerns a protected resting place, unrelated to the focus.
Divine awareness of conduct in an interpersonal case is too general to add much.
Adds that a community's current practice can be void, sharpening the danger of inherited arrangements.
Divine encompassing of deeds appears in a different admonition and is redundant.
Disavowal of others' deeds does not develop succession or divine examination.
The contextual use of 'after' and 'waiting' is unrelated to the focus's generational transition.
A later bestowal and prophetic appointment does not materially illuminate successor responsibility.
Knowledge of the hereafter is unrelated to earthly succession or assessed action.
Links faithful righteous action to a transformed outcome, a broad but coherent responsibility parallel.
Adds recurring alternation among communities and a discriminating divine knowing, without the earthly-successor wording.
Explicit removal-and-replacement route that makes continued communal standing non-automatic.
Adds replacement by a differently characterized people following abandonment of the required commitment.
Directly combines removal with making successors after those removed.
Directly frames the earth as inherited by whom God wills and calls for a patient moral response.
Narrates inheritance of the land by the formerly oppressed after the prior power is ended.
Adds a moral condition to the continuance or reversal of a community's received favor.
Explicitly makes refusal open a replacement-by-another-people route.
Sets reform within a community against its ruin, clarifying the conduct at stake in historical continuation.
Pairs establishment in the earth with beneficence and the non-loss of the doers' reward.
Adds a community-level change principle tied to what people alter in themselves.
States the remove-and-bring-another-creation possibility, though without the focus's concrete successor scene.
Provides a settled community's reversal after its response to provision, a secondary warning about inherited conditions.
Begins a recurrent corruption-and-consequence cycle for a people in the land.
Completes that cycle with reversal after renewed corruption, preserving both adverse and renewed readings.
Adds a destruction pattern for a town after corrupt conduct, but not a later successor's examination.
Earthly empowerment supplies a secondary stewardship setting without a generational transfer.
Directly joins inheritance of the earth to a qualified servant community.
Makes earthly empowerment answerable through a specified public pattern of conduct.
Narrates inheritance by another people after the former possessors are displaced.
Pairs empowerment and establishment in the earth for the oppressed with a disclosed outcome for the former rulers.
Adds destruction of prosperous settlements, but not the successor or action-test side.
Collects distinct wrongdoing-and-consequence cases, supporting the prior-generation background only.
Another dwelling-trace lesson from destroyed generations, redundant with 20:128.
Records inheritance of land, homes, and goods after a prior group, a concrete transfer scene.
Explicitly holds removal and replacement with a new creation as an open possibility.
Directly couples khalifah in the earth with just judgment and a prohibition on desire-led conduct.
Reiterates destruction of earlier, stronger people without a successor responsibility component.

Explicitly warns that turning away can bring replacement by another people with a different response.
A further stronger-generation destruction case, redundant with the existing outcome evidence.
Adds communal reckoning and consequence for disobedient towns, secondary to the succession frame.
States the possibility of replacing a people with their like, but outside the earthly inheritance setting.
